hud.head: HEAD
hud.contextButtonsNote: PROPOSED labels: the design says only 'J/K/L/U by context'. Keys are input actions j/k/l/u (Button 1/2/3/Grab). Replace with whatever the engine binds; '-' = unused.

FLY.label: Flyweight
FLY.blurb: Fastest division. Low power, high pace.

HW.label: Heavyweight
HW.blurb: Slow, huge power, low cardio. One shot changes everything.

BOX.label: Boxing
BOX.blurb: Best hands and head movement. Hook-uppercut power chain and a better perfect-block window. Weak kicks and ground game.

MT.label: Muay Thai
MT.blurb: Teep, leg kicks, elbows, knees, and the Thai clinch. The art of eight limbs.

WR.label: Wrestling
WR.blurb: Fast, hard-to-stop takedowns, chain re-shots, the best sprawl, and the easiest path to mount.

BJJ.label: Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu
BJJ.blurb: Guard pulls, sweeps, fast back takes, and an edge in every submission. Weakest striking.

PRESSURE.label: Pressure Brawler
PRESSURE.blurb: Big chin, big power. Walks forward. Gasses out.

COUNTER.label: Counter-Striker
COUNTER.blurb: Wider perfect-block window and a counter bonus. Low output.

VOLUME.label: Volume All-Rounder
VOLUME.blurb: Elite cardio, steady output, no glaring holes.

SMOTHER.label: Smother Grappler
SMOTHER.blurb: Strong and heavy. Chains takedowns and grinds out control.

CREATIVE.label: Creative / Unorthodox
CREATIVE.blurb: Long reach, odd angles, spinning shots. Inconsistent defense.

grappling.blurb: Takedowns, ground control, and the submission tug-of-war.

strength.blurb: Clinch control, escapes, and holding position.

screen.title: Controls
screen.contextNote: Buttons change labels in the clinch and on the ground. Watch the button text.

steps.title: Welcome to the Cage
steps.text: This is the AFL. Two fighters, one cage, three rounds. The clock shows 5:00 but runs fast: each round lasts one real minute. Let's learn how to win.

steps.title: Footwork
steps.text: Use {btnMove} to step in and out of range. Moving also lets your stamina recover.

steps.title: The Jab
steps.text: Press {btnJab} to jab. It's fast and cheap on stamina. Use it to measure distance and keep your opponent honest.

steps.title: Power Strike
steps.text: Press {btnPower} for a power strike. Slow, big damage, big stamina cost. Don't throw it at air.

steps.title: Kicks
steps.text: Press {btnKick} to kick from range. Kicks reach far, but a body kick can be caught, and a caught kick gives your opponent a free takedown attempt.

steps.title: Going Low
steps.text: Hold {btnLow} while you strike to go low. Low kicks build leg damage: a hurt leg moves slowly, kicks weakly, and can drop you.

steps.title: Teep (Muay Thai)
steps.text: Muay Thai fighters can hold {btnForward} and press {btnKick} for a teep: a push kick that breaks pressure and drains stamina.

steps.title: Blocking
steps.text: Hold {btnBlock} to guard high. Hold {btnBlock} + {btnLow} to guard low. Each blocked hit costs a little stamina.

steps.title: Check the Leg Kick
steps.text: Guard low ({btnBlock} + {btnLow}) against a leg kick to check it. The kicker hurts his own leg.

steps.title: Perfect Block
steps.text: Press {btnBlock} just before a strike lands for a perfect block. Your attacker staggers, and that's your opening. Perfect-block a body kick to catch it.

steps.title: Stamina Is Everything
steps.text: Every action drains your stamina bar. Low stamina means slower strikes, weaker blocks, and easier takedowns. Stay idle or move to recover; you get a partial refill between rounds.

steps.title: Damage
steps.text: Head damage builds toward a knockout. Body damage lowers your max stamina. Leg damage slows you down. Watch the face, body, and leg meters.

steps.title: Fight Back or Get Stopped
steps.text: Eat clean shots without blocking, escaping, or hitting back and the referee's meter fills. When it's full, he stops the fight. Defend or answer to drain it.

steps.title: The Clinch
steps.text: Get close and press {btnGrab} to clinch. Inside, use {btnClinchStrike} for short strikes, {btnClinchKnee} for knees, or {btnClinchBreak} to break away. Escaping is a timing battle, and Strength helps.
steps.goal: Land a knee from the clinch.

steps.title: Takedowns
steps.text: From mid-range, press {btnTakedown} to shoot. Land it and you're on top in your opponent's guard.

steps.title: Stopping Takedowns
steps.text: When they shoot, hold {btnLow} to sprawl, time a knee, or press {btnGrab} for a guillotine.

steps.title: The Ground Ladder
steps.text: On the ground, position is a ladder: Guard, then Mount, then Back. The higher you climb on top, the more danger you put your opponent in. Buttons change on the ground, so watch their labels.

steps.title: Top in Guard
steps.text: From top guard, {btnGroundStrike} for ground and pound, {btnGroundElbow} for elbows, or {btnAdvance} to pass to mount. Strikes from inside the guard do less damage.

steps.title: Bottom in Guard
steps.text: From guard: block, {btnScramble} to get up, {btnSweep} to sweep to top, or {btnSubmit} for an armbar or triangle.

steps.title: Mount
steps.text: Mount is the heaviest ground and pound, 12-6 elbows included. Press {btnSubmit} for an armbar, or {btnAdvance} to take the back when your opponent turns away. Stuck on the bottom? Press {btnBridge} to bridge back to guard.
steps.goal: Land ground and pound from mount.

steps.title: Back Control
steps.text: On the back, {btnSubmit} goes for the rear-naked choke. If your back is taken, use {btnHandFight} to fight the hands and escape to guard.

steps.title: Keep Working
steps.text: Stall on the ground and the referee yells "Work!" Keep stalling and he stands you both up.

steps.title: Submissions
steps.text: Every submission is a tug-of-war. Tap {btnSubTug} in rhythm to win it. Grappling and stamina tip the scale.

steps.title: How Fights End
steps.text: KO: head health hits zero. TKO: the referee's meter fills, or a fighter is too hurt to answer the bell. Submission: they tap. Otherwise, three judges score every round: damage first, then aggression, then control.

steps.title: Your Corner
steps.text: Between rounds, your corner shows your stamina, damage, a scorecard estimate, and one tip. Tap to skip it.

steps.title: Your Discipline
steps.text: Each discipline adds signature moves: Boxing chains hooks and uppercuts, Muay Thai adds teeps, elbows, and the Thai clinch, Wrestling shoots faster and climbs to mount easier, and BJJ can pull guard with {btnTakedown}.

steps.title: Take a Breath
steps.text: Press {btnPause} any time to pause and review the controls.

steps.title: You're Ready
steps.text: That's the basics. Fight smart, manage your stamina, and finish when you see the opening. Good luck, champ.

disciplineTips.BOX: Your power strike chains hooks and uppercuts, and your perfect-block window is wider. Win on the feet; stay off the mat.
disciplineTips.MT: Teep to stop pressure, chop the legs, and look for elbows up close. In the clinch, your knees are deadly.
disciplineTips.WR: Your takedowns are fast and hard to stop, and you climb to mount easier than anyone. If a shot fails, shoot again.
disciplineTips.BJJ: Pull guard with {btnTakedown}, sweep, take the back, and win every submission battle. Don't trade on the feet.

careerIntro.title: Welcome to the AFL
careerIntro.text: You're an unknown with a gym bag and a dream. Win fights, climb the rankings, and take the belt.

careerIntro.title: Training Camp
careerIntro.text: Between fights you get about six weeks of camp. Each week, tap one focus, or let Auto-Plan do it. Training raises stats but adds fatigue, so rest when you need it. Stats never decay.

careerIntro.title: Cross-Training
careerIntro.text: Train another discipline's sessions to unlock one of its signature moves.

careerIntro.title: Fight Offers
careerIntro.text: Each cycle brings two or three offers. Every card shows the opponent, purse, possible rank jump, hype, and camp length. Short-notice fights mean half a camp, but more hype and money.

careerIntro.title: Rivals Remember
careerIntro.text: The AFL's star fighters remember how your fights ended. Beat one close, and they'll be back for a rematch.

careerIntro.title: Rankings
careerIntro.text: Each division has a champion and a top 10. Ranked wins and finishes move you up faster. Losses move you down.

careerIntro.title: The Title
careerIntro.text: Reach #1, or #3 on a finishing streak, to earn a five-round title fight. Win it, defend it, and retire a king.

loadingTips: Stamina is everything. Swing wild and you gas out.
A perfect block staggers your attacker. Make them pay.
Leg kicks add up. Enough of them and your opponent can't stand.
Body damage lowers max stamina. Go to the body early.
Kicks can be caught. Mix them up.
Sprawl by blocking low when they shoot.
Time a knee as they shoot for a takedown.
Never give up your back to a BJJ fighter.
Eat unanswered shots and the ref will stop it. Block, move, or hit back.
Judges score damage first, then aggression, then control.
Rest weeks matter. Tired fighters lose.
Short-notice fights pay more, but you'll have less time to prepare.
Finishes move you up the rankings faster than decisions.
Title fights are five rounds. Train your cardio.
Low stamina makes you easier to take down.
Check leg kicks by guarding low. The kicker pays for it.
Stall on the ground and the ref will stand you up.
Mount means heavy ground and pound. Bridge out fast.
12-6 elbows are legal on the ground.
